decisions.title: Accepted proposals: providing a TYPE_CHECKING shim for third-party decorators and adopting the main @typing.override decorator
reasons: One way of handling this kind of thing is to do a typing.TYPE_CHECKING shim, like so: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING if TYPE_CHECKING: from typing import override as override else: def override(func):
The SC has decided to accept this PEP!

similarRejected.title: Rejecting built-in runtime enforcement or parent-class specification due to low utility and library-level implementability
reasons: if in a single commit you move a method from one base to another, you as the author are likely aware of what you did, so the safety benefits are relatively small

I'm guessing there wouldn't be too much use of this feature. Since it's relatively easy to implement this capability using runtime logic in a library, that makes me thing we don't need to bake it into typing.py all of the type checkers.

similarRejected.title: Requiring the decorator specifically for abstract method overrides (rejected in favor of a strict mode option)
reasons: I'm not sure there is much need for special treatment of abstract methods. The PEP recommends type checkers support a strict mode where all method overrides must be marked with the decorator, whether abstract or not.
